title: Shop — Redis
description: Redis with Sentinel: master and failover readiness, failovers, replication, memory and evictions, server and client latency, connection pools, the notification stream, persistence and the Sentinel logs.

list.name: Redis master changes
list.expr: max by (pod) (redis_instance_info{job="redis-node", role="master"}) unless max by (pod) (redis_instance_info{job="redis-node", role="master"} offset 1m)

list.name: Critical alerts
list.expr: max by (alertname, job, deployment, slo) (ALERTS{alertname=~"Shop.*", alertstate="firing", severity="critical"})

list.name: Node restarts
list.expr: (max by (node) (label_replace(node_boot_time_seconds, "internal_ip", "$1", "instance", "(.+):[0-9]+") * on (internal_ip) group_left (node) max by (internal_ip, node) (kube_node_info)) > max_over_time((max by (node) (label_replace(node_boot_time_seconds, "internal_ip", "$1", "instance", "(.+):[0-9]+") * on (internal_ip) group_left (node) max by (internal_ip, node) (kube_node_info)))[30m:1m] offset 1m)) * on (node) group_left (label_cloud_google_com_gke_nodepool, label_cloud_google_com_gke_provisioning) max by (node, label_cloud_google_com_gke_nodepool, label_cloud_google_com_gke_provisioning) (kube_node_labels)
list.textFormat: Pool {{label_cloud_google_com_gke_nodepool}} ({{label_cloud_google_com_gke_provisioning}}): spot preemption, upgrade or repair; its pods were rescheduled

list.name: Container restarts
list.expr: (changes(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="shop"}[1m]) > 0) * on (namespace, pod, container) group_left (reason) max by (namespace, pod, container, reason) (kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{namespace="shop"})

panels.title: Overview — is Redis healthy, and could it fail over right now?
Master
panels.description: The pod that takes the writes now. Clients find it through Sentinel (service redis-sentinel).

panels.title: Failover possible
panels.description: SENTINEL CKQUORUM: enough sentinels (2 of 3) agree to promote a replica if the master fails. No means the next master failure is an outage.

panels.title: Healthy sentinels
panels.description: Sentinels the least informed sentinel sees as healthy (of 3). Quorum is 2: at 2 one more lost node blocks failovers.

panels.title: Replicas in sync
panels.description: Replicas with a live replication link to the master (of 2): the failover candidates.

panels.title: Failovers
panels.description: Completed failovers in the time range (logged by the sentinel that led them). Each one fails writes for a few seconds; annotations mark when.

panels.title: Sentinel TILT events
panels.description: Times a sentinel entered TILT (clock jump or stalled process, usually CPU starvation): for 30s it authorises no failover.

panels.title: Commands / s
panels.description: Commands processed by all nodes (replication traffic included).

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Key lookups that found the key, over the time range (user and product cache reads, idempotency checks).

panels.title: Memory of maxmemory
panels.description: The master's dataset against maxmemory (96mb). At 100% keys with a TTL are evicted, then writes fail with OOM.

targets.expr: max((redis_memory_used_bytes{job="redis-node"} / redis_memory_max_bytes{job="redis-node"}) * on (pod) group_left () max by (pod) (redis_instance_info{job="redis-node", role="master"}))

panels.title: Evicted keys
panels.description: Keys removed for memory in the time range: cache entries and payment idempotency keys.

panels.title: Client p99 latency
panels.description: 99th percentile of every Redis call as the services measure it (spans): network, pool wait and Redis together.

panels.title: Notification backlog
panels.description: Notifications in the stream not yet read by the notifier group.

panels.title: Nodes
panels.description: Every Redis pod: its node, role, replication link and how many bytes it is behind the master, clients, memory, fragmentation (RSS / used: above 1.5 wastes RAM once the dataset is large; below ~100 MB the allocator's fixed overhead makes it high and meaningless), uptime, and what the sentinel in the same pod believes: which master it follows, whether that master is ok, how many sentinels it sees healthy, TILT. All sentinels must follow the same master (RedisSentinelsDisagree).

targets.expr: clamp_min(scalar(max(redis_master_repl_offset{job="redis-node"} * on (pod) group_left () max by (pod) (redis_instance_info{job="redis-node", role="master"}))) - max by (pod) (redis_master_repl_offset{job="redis-node"}), 0)

panels.title: Role over time
panels.description: Which pod was master when: a change of colour between pods is a failover.

targets.expr: max by (pod) (redis_instance_info{job="redis-node", role="master"}) * 2 or max by (pod) (redis_instance_info{job="redis-node", role="slave"}) or max by (pod) (redis_up{job="redis-node"}) * 0

panels.title: Sentinel events
panels.description: What the sentinels decided: +sdown (one sentinel lost contact for 5s), +odown (the quorum agrees the master is down), +try-failover / +elected-leader / +selected-slave / +promoted-slave, +switch-master (clients now go to the new master), +tilt, -failover-abort-* (no replica could be promoted).

panels.title: Bytes behind the master
panels.description: Replication offset of each replica against the master's: what a failover to that pod would lose. Normally a few bytes (scrapes of the pods are a few seconds apart).

targets.expr: clamp_min(scalar(max(redis_master_repl_offset{job="redis-node"} * on (pod) group_left () max by (pod) (redis_instance_info{job="redis-node", role="master"}))) - max by (pod) (redis_master_repl_offset{job="redis-node"}), 0)

panels.title: Replica acknowledgement lag
panels.description: Seconds since each replica last acknowledged the stream from the master (RedisReplicaLagging above 10s).

panels.title: Resyncs
panels.description: Replicas reconnecting: partial (from the backlog) is cheap; full copies the whole dataset (after a restart, a failover, or a backlog too small for the outage).

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Redis' own memory per pod against maxmemory (evictions start there) and the container's working set against its limit (the kernel OOM-kills there): replication and client buffers and the AOF rewrite fork sit between the two.

panels.title: Evicted and expired keys
panels.description: Keys per second removed for memory (evicted: should be 0) and at the end of their TTL (expired: normal cache turnover).

panels.title: Keys
panels.description: Keys on the master; only those with a TTL can be evicted (volatile-lru). The notification stream has none.

targets.expr: max((sum by (pod) (redis_db_keys{job="redis-node"})) * on (pod) group_left () max by (pod) (redis_instance_info{job="redis-node", role="master"}))
max((sum by (pod) (redis_db_keys_expiring{job="redis-node"})) * on (pod) group_left () max by (pod) (redis_instance_info{job="redis-node", role="master"}))

panels.title: Commands and latency — the server side
Commands by command
panels.description: Top commands per second on all nodes (replicas run the replicated writes).

panels.title: Server latency p99 by command
panels.description: Time Redis spends executing each command (LATENCY HISTOGRAM, since start). Compare with the client latency below: the difference is network and pool waiting.

targets.expr: max by (cmd) (redis_latency_percentiles_usec{job="redis-node", quantile="99"}) and on (cmd) topk(8, sum by (cmd) (rate(redis_commands_total{job="redis-node"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Errors and rejections
panels.description: Error replies by type: OOM (memory full), READONLY (write on a replica, during a failover), LOADING (replica loading its data), NOAUTH (client before AUTH), BUSYGROUP (the stream group exists, harmless at service start).

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Client connections per pod (the services' pools, sentinels, replicas, the exporter); blocked: clients waiting in XREADGROUP BLOCK.

panels.title: Slow log
panels.description: Commands slower than slowlog-log-slower-than (10ms): entries kept (left) and the duration of the last one (right). redis-cli SLOWLOG GET shows them.

panels.title: Client latency p99 by service and command
panels.description: 99th percentile of the Redis calls as each service sees them (redisotel spans): includes network and waiting for a pooled connection.

targets.expr: "resource_attr:service.namespace":=shop "span_attr:db.system":=redis | copy "resource_attr:service.name" as service | stats by (service, name) quantile(0.99, duration) p99

panels.title: Client calls and errors
panels.description: Redis calls per interval by service (left) and the failed ones (right): connection errors and READONLY during a failover, timeouts.

targets.expr: "resource_attr:service.namespace":=shop "span_attr:db.system":=redis | copy "resource_attr:service.name" as service | stats by (service) count() calls
"resource_attr:service.namespace":=shop "span_attr:db.system":=redis status_code:=2 | copy "resource_attr:service.name" as service | stats by (service) count() errors

panels.title: Connection pools: in use against the pool size
panels.description: Connections each service's go-redis pool has busy, against REDIS_POOL_SIZE. The stream consumer keeps one in XREADGROUP BLOCK.

panels.title: Pool waits and timeouts
panels.description: Commands per second that waited for a free connection, failed waiting (RedisClientPoolTimeouts), and broken connections thrown away (expected right after a failover).

panels.title: Slowest Redis calls
panels.description: The 20 slowest Redis calls in the time range; open the trace to see what waited.

targets.expr: "resource_attr:service.namespace":=shop "span_attr:db.system":=redis | copy "resource_attr:service.name" as service | copy "span_attr:db.statement" as statement | stats by (trace_id, service, name, statement) max(duration) took | sort by (took desc) | limit 20

panels.title: Stream and the notifier group
panels.description: The notifications stream (MAXLEN ~10000, so the length stays near 10000): entries the group has not read yet, entries delivered but never acknowledged (a consumer died mid-delivery; nothing reclaims them), and the enqueue rate (right).

targets.expr: max((redis_stream_length{job="redis-node", stream="notifications"}) * on (pod) group_left () max by (pod) (redis_instance_info{job="redis-node", role="master"}))
max((redis_stream_group_lag{job="redis-node", stream="notifications"}) * on (pod) group_left () max by (pod) (redis_instance_info{job="redis-node", role="master"}))
max((redis_stream_group_messages_pending{job="redis-node", stream="notifications"}) * on (pod) group_left () max by (pod) (redis_instance_info{job="redis-node", role="master"}))

panels.title: Consumers
panels.description: Consumers of the notifier group. A live pod polls every 5s (idle < 5s); a long idle consumer is a pod that is gone (rescheduled), and its pending entries are never delivered. Remove it with XGROUP DELCONSUMER once it has none.

targets.expr: max by (consumer) (redis_stream_group_consumer_idle_seconds{job="redis-node", stream="notifications"} * on (pod) group_left () max by (pod) (redis_instance_info{job="redis-node", role="master"}))
max by (consumer) (redis_stream_group_consumer_messages_pending{job="redis-node", stream="notifications"} * on (pod) group_left () max by (pod) (redis_instance_info{job="redis-node", role="master"}))

panels.title: Append-only file
panels.description: AOF size per pod (appendfsync everysec); a rewrite compacts it in a forked child (memory copy-on-write: RedisContainerMemoryNearLimit).

panels.title: AOF health
panels.description: 1 = the last AOF write and rewrite succeeded. A failed write makes Redis refuse writes (RedisPersistenceFailing). Delayed fsyncs: the disk is slower than the write rate.

panels.title: Data volumes
panels.description: Used share of each pod's data volume (AOF and its rewrites).

panels.title: Redis and Sentinel logs
panels.description: Warnings (#) and notices of Redis and Sentinel, routine replication and AOF lines left out.

targets.expr: {kubernetes.pod_namespace="shop", kubernetes.container_name=~"redis|sentinel"} _msg:~" [#!*] " -_msg:~"Background AOF|AOF rewrite|Accepted|Synchronization with replica|Streamed RDB|MASTER <-> REPLICA sync|Diskless" | format "<kubernetes.pod_name>/<kubernetes.container_name>: <_msg>" as _msg

panels.title: go-redis client messages in the services
panels.description: What the clients logged: Sentinel discovering a new master, pool timeouts, READONLY writes during a failover. go-redis logs through its own logger, so these lines have no service or level field.
